subject.title: fix: external plugin tabs fail under gateway auth

question: Must plugin-tab iframe authorization be route- and revocation-bound, or is an origin-wide five-minute operator cookie an acceptable Gateway security contract?
rationale: The linked bug requires a browser credential handoff, but choosing the permanent breadth and revocation semantics of that credential changes the Gateway authentication boundary and cannot be safely inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Require a scoped launch grant
options.body: Mint a grant for the selected registered route prefix and current auth generation so credential rotation, device revocation, and cross-plugin requests invalidate or reject it.

options.title: Accept the origin-wide cookie
options.body: Explicitly approve a reusable five-minute operator grant across protected plugin routes and document the residual revocation and cross-route exposure.

options.title: Pause the iframe handoff
options.body: Keep gateway-authenticated external tabs unsupported until a narrower browser-auth architecture is agreed.

recommendation.title: Require a scoped launch grant
recommendation.body: Mint a grant for the selected registered route prefix and current auth generation so credential rotation, device revocation, and cross-plugin requests invalidate or reject it.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged gateway-auth scope work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the security-boundary decision.
